transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been getting kind of fixated on my face. We put in a brighter bathroom mirror, and now I keep noticing the skin around my cheeks and jaw looking uneven or saggy. My husband says he doesn’t really see it, but… I do.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t know… not really, I guess. I’ve been a little preoccupied, but I wouldn’t say hopeless or anything.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking the mirror, touching your face, or comparing yourself to others, because of how you feel about your appearance?

Yeah… I mean, I do check the mirror most mornings, probably more than I need to. I’ll look from a few angles and usually put on a little extra makeup before I leave for the courthouse.

And… sometimes I catch myself comparing my face to women at work. I also try to stay out of casual pictures if I’m not feeling okay about how I look.
Does this concern about your face cause you any distress, or affect your daily activities in any way?

A little, yeah. I mean, I still get my work done… it’s not like I can’t function. But I’ve been taking longer to get ready, so I’ve rushed into the courthouse late a few mornings.

And I’ve missed the start of yoga more than once. I also… avoid some casual photos at book club or community things if I’m worried about how my face will look.
Do you feel anxious or distressed when you can’t check your face, or worry something bad might happen if you don’t look a certain way?

I don’t think I worry something bad will happen, exactly. It’s more… I feel unsettled if I leave without checking. Most mornings I look at my face from a few angles and add a little more makeup before I go to the courthouse.

And if I’m already feeling off about it, I might compare myself to women at work or just avoid being in casual pictures.
When you look at your face and feel concerned about how it looks, is your main worry that others will judge you negatively or that something is medically or cosmetically wrong with your face itself?

It’s more that it feels like something looks wrong with my face itself, I guess. Since we got that brighter bathroom mirror, I keep noticing my cheeks and jaw… like the skin looks uneven or a little saggy to me.

My husband says he doesn’t really see it, but I do.
Have you ever had sudden, intrusive thoughts about your face that you can’t seem to get out of your head, even if you know they might not make sense?

I mean… not sudden exactly. It’s more that since we put in that brighter bathroom mirror, I keep noticing my cheeks and jaw. The skin looks uneven, or kind of saggy to me.

My husband says he doesn’t really see it, so… I know maybe it’s not obvious. But I still notice it.
Do you believe that the unevenness or saggy skin you see on your cheeks and jaw is something that should be noticeable to others, or is it something only you seem to notice?
I guess… it seems like mostly I’m the one noticing it. I feel like the skin around my cheeks and jaw looks uneven or a little saggy, but my husband says he can’t really see what I mean.
Are you also worried about other things in your life besides your face — like work, family, or other responsibilities — or is your main concern about how your face looks?

Mostly it’s my face. I mean, I have normal worries, but I’m here because since we got that brighter bathroom mirror, I keep seeing the skin around my cheeks and jaw looking uneven or kind of saggy… even though my husband says he doesn’t really see it.
Do you feel that the way your cheeks and jaw look is something that is truly abnormal or defective, even if others don’t see it that way?

I don’t know if I’d say “truly defective.” It’s just… when I look in that brighter mirror, the skin around my cheeks and jaw looks uneven, kind of saggy to me. My husband says he doesn’t really see it, so maybe it’s just me, but I keep noticing it.

When you look at your face and see the unevenness or sagging around your cheeks and jaw, do you believe this is something that others should be able to see and would agree with you if they looked closely enough, or do you think it’s something only you can perceive in a way that others don’t?

I think… it’s probably mostly me seeing it. Since we put in that brighter bathroom mirror, I keep noticing my cheeks and jaw looking uneven or kind of saggy, but my husband says he can’t really see what I’m talking about.

When you notice the unevenness or sagging around your cheeks and jaw, does it feel like a minor issue that others would hardly notice, or does it feel so significant to you that you can’t stop thinking about it, even if you know it might not make sense?

It feels… bigger to me than it probably is. I know my husband says he can’t really see it, but since we put in that brighter mirror, I keep noticing the skin around my cheeks and jaw looking uneven or a little saggy. It’s hard not to focus on it.

When you look at your cheeks and jaw and notice the unevenness or sagging, do you feel like this is something that others would barely notice or not agree with you about, even though it feels very real and upsetting to you?

Yeah… I think other people probably wouldn’t really notice it. My husband says he can’t see what I’m talking about. But when I look in that brighter mirror, I keep seeing my cheeks and jaw looking uneven or kind of saggy, and it just feels really hard to ignore.
